title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #9

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The touch-me-not plant folds its leaves when touched. This shows that plants can (1 mark)
   A. respond to changes
   B. move from place to place
   C. lay eggs
   D. eat food

2. What do fish use to take oxygen from water? (1 mark)
   A. Lungs
   B. Gills
   C. Feathers
   D. Horns

3. What is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal that flies
   B. An animal without a backbone
   C. An animal with a backbone
   D. An animal with hair

4. How do young mammals get their first food? (1 mark)
   A. By hunting
   B. By drinking their mother's milk
   C. By eating grass
   D. By eating stones

5. Which of these animals is an amphibian? (1 mark)
   A. Toad
   B. Goat
   C. Snake
   D. Tortoise

6. Which of these is a crab? (1 mark)
   A. A bird
   B. A mammal
   C. A vertebrate with fur
   D. An invertebrate with a hard outer shell

7. Why should fruits and vegetables be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To remove dirt and germs
   B. To make them heavier
   C. To make them sweeter
   D. To make them hot

8. Why are solids like bricks and stones used to build houses? (1 mark)
   A. They are invisible
   B. They spread out
   C. They keep their shape and can support weight
   D. They flow easily

9. Which of these is heavier: 3 kg of sugar or 3000 g of sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Cannot tell
   B. 3000 g
   C. They have the same mass
   D. 3 kg

10. Which of these is a correct grouping? (1 mark)
   A. Chalk, water and steam are solids
   B. Milk, water and juice are liquids
   C. Air, stone and salt are gases
   D. Steam, oil and rice are gases

11. How many millilitres are in 2 litres? (1 mark)
   A. 200
   B. 2000
   C. 20
   D. 20 000

12. What happens to a liquid when you pour it into a different container? (1 mark)
   A. It disappears
   B. It keeps its old shape
   C. It takes the shape of the new container
   D. It becomes a solid

13. A heavy sack of maize has more mass than a small packet of salt. This means the sack has more (1 mark)
   A. Air only
   B. Matter
   C. Sound
   D. Light

14. Which waste can be reused as a pencil holder? (1 mark)
   A. An empty tin
   B. Old leaves
   C. Banana peel
   D. Egg shells

15. A pupil wants to make a toy car from waste. Which materials are suitable? (1 mark)
   A. A box and bottle tops
   B. Water and air
   C. Banana peel and leaves
   D. Fire and paper

16. Why is waste in rivers dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It makes fish bigger
   B. It makes rain
   C. It makes water clean
   D. It makes water dirty and harms fish

17. Which of these makes a good compost mixture? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetable peelings, dry leaves and some soil
   B. Glass and metal
   C. Plastic and tins
   D. Batteries and plastic

18. What is the danger of leaving plastic bags on the ground? (1 mark)
   A. They stay for a long time and block drains
   B. They turn into soil fast
   C. They grow into plants
   D. They make the soil rich

19. Which of these is an example of reusing water? (1 mark)
   A. Pouring water down the drain
   B. Leaving taps open
   C. Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   D. Buying bottled water

20. Which of these is a source of dirty water we should not drink? (1 mark)
   A. Clean tap water
   B. Boiled and treated water
   C. Water used to wash clothes
   D. Safe borehole water

21. Which force slows down or stops a book sliding on the floor? (1 mark)
   A. Friction
   B. Heat
   C. Gravity
   D. Light

22. A cyclist pedals harder and goes faster. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Increases speed
   B. Changes shape
   C. Stops motion
   D. Decreases speed

23. A cyclist presses the brakes and slows down. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Holds objects together
   B. Increases speed
   C. Decreases speed
   D. Starts motion

24. A ball is rolling and you kick it in the direction it moves. What happens? (1 mark)
   A. It changes into a solid
   B. It speeds up
   C. It gets smaller
   D. It stops

25. Which of these gives artificial light by burning paraffin? (1 mark)
   A. Sun
   B. Lightning
   C. Star
   D. Paraffin lamp

26. What do reflectors on a road or bicycle do? (1 mark)
   A. Shine when car lights fall on them
   B. Make sound
   C. Make their own light all night
   D. Make heat

27. Why do some farmers use bright lights near animal pens at night? (1 mark)
   A. To make animals heavier
   B. To make animals sleepy
   C. To scare away wild animals
   D. To warm animals

28. Which of these is an artificial source of light? (1 mark)
   A. Stars
   B. Lightning
   C. The sun
   D. Electric bulb

29. Which of these gives out heat when rubbed? (1 mark)
   A. A stone table
   B. A book in a bag
   C. Hands
   D. A leaf

30. What does a mother hen do for her chicks? (1 mark)
   A. Cools them
   B. Keeps them warm under her wings
   C. Makes them wet
   D. Feeds them iron

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why burning waste is not a good way of managing waste and give better methods. (5 marks)

32. Explain how light helps in security and safety. Give three examples. (3 marks)

33. Classify these as natural or artificial: candle, stars, torch, lightning, firefly, solar lamp. (4 marks)

34. Give three problems caused by friction. (3 marks)

35. Describe the natural and artificial sources of light and explain the difference. (5 marks)

36. Discuss how a family can light their home cheaply and safely. (5 marks)

37. State two uses of heat at home. (2 marks)

38. Write three safety rules when observing animals in the school compound. (3 marks)

39. Give three examples where a force holds objects together. (3 marks)

40. Draw a simple diagram of the digestive system and label mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine and anus. (5 marks)

41. Give three ways of caring for animals. (3 marks)

42. Explain how wasting water can affect other people and the family. (4 marks)

43. Why should you wear gloves when collecting waste? (2 marks)

44. Name three gases and say how each is useful. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — respond to changes
   Folding when touched is a response to a change in the surroundings.

2. B — Gills
   Fish breathe using gills.

3. B — An animal without a backbone
   Invertebrates have no backbone.

4. B — By drinking their mother's milk
   Mammals feed their babies with milk.

5. A — Toad
   Toads have moist skin and start life in water.

6. D — An invertebrate with a hard outer shell
   A crab has no backbone and has a hard shell outside.

7. A — To remove dirt and germs
   Washing removes dirt, germs and worm eggs.

8. C — They keep their shape and can support weight
   Solids keep their shape.

9. C — They have the same mass
   3 kg equals 3000 g.

10. B — Milk, water and juice are liquids
   Milk, water and juice are all liquids.

11. B — 2000
   2 x 1000 = 2000 ml.

12. C — It takes the shape of the new container
   A liquid has no shape of its own.

13. B — Matter
   Mass is the amount of matter.

14. A — An empty tin
   A clean tin can be reused.

15. A — A box and bottle tops
   A box and bottle tops make a toy car.

16. D — It makes water dirty and harms fish
   Waste pollutes water and harms living things.

17. A — Vegetable peelings, dry leaves and some soil
   Composting uses natural plant waste.

18. A — They stay for a long time and block drains
   Plastic bags stay for years and block drains.

19. C — Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   Using water twice is reusing.

20. C — Water used to wash clothes
   Used washing water is dirty and unsafe.

21. A — Friction
   Friction opposes the movement between surfaces.

22. A — Increases speed
   More force increases speed.

23. C — Decreases speed
   Brakes use friction to slow the bicycle.

24. B — It speeds up
   A force in the direction of movement increases speed.

25. D — Paraffin lamp
   A paraffin lamp is a made light source.

26. A — Shine when car lights fall on them
   Reflectors bounce light back.

27. C — To scare away wild animals
   Bright lights can scare away predators.

28. D — Electric bulb
   Bulbs are made by people.

29. C — Hands
   Rubbing produces heat through friction.

30. B — Keeps them warm under her wings
   Chicks need warmth.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Burning gives harmful smoke, especially from plastic. Better: reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and use bins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for better methods.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Street lights help people see, security lights keep thieves away, traffic lights direct drivers, torches show dangers, reflectors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Natural: stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: candle, torch, solar lamp.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair, plus 1 mark for correct table.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It wears away shoes and tyres, wastes energy, makes machines hot and slows moving parts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Natural sources are found in nature such as the sun, stars, lightning and fireflies. Artificial sources are made by people such as bulbs, torches and candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for natural and artificial, 1 mark for examples of each and 1 mark for the difference.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use windows and translucent sheets by day, solar lamps and LED bulbs at night, keep candles and paraffin away from cloth, turn off lights when not needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cooking, warming, ironing, drying clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not pick up animals you do not know, do not harm animals, wash hands after touching soil or animals, return animals to where they were found.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Glue holding paper, nails holding wood, rope tying things, stitches holding cloth, screws.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: A neat tube drawn from mouth to anus with each part labelled in the correct order.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drawing and 1 mark for each of four correct labels.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide shelter, keep their homes clean, treat sick animals, do not beat them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Less water is left for others, especially in dry areas. The family pays more for water and may have to fetch more.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for others and 2 marks for family.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: To protect your hands from cuts and germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cuts and 1 mark for germs.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Air or oxygen for breathing, cooking gas for cooking, air in tyres or footballs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each gas with its use.
